_about: Published card-counting systems, compiled 2026-09-28 by a Claude Code research workflow. One sweep read the reference tables (QFIT and Modern Blackjack, blackjackreview's comparison table, Wizard of Odds, Wikipedia, Blackjack Apprenticeship, BlackjackInfo's efficiency calculator). A second sweep of the originators' own publications stalled and never reported, so the reconciling agent checked every system against a second source itself, fetching the authors' own texts where it could (Snyder on Red 7 and Hi-Lo Lite, Vancura and Fuchs on KO, Wattenberger on REKO and FELT, Victor, Harris on the BRH counts, Renzey on KISS). A system is listed only when two sources agree on its tags or its author published them; the rest are under 'excluded' with the reason. 'tags' are per rank as published, T being every ten-valued card; where a count depends on suit or face, 'cardTags' gives the real tags ('2red', '7black', '10', 'J', ...) and 'tags' holds their average. 'count' is the author's conversion where the sources state one, otherwise 'true' for a balanced count and 'running' for an unbalanced one. The text fields are the sources' words, summarised, including what could not be confirmed.

systems.name: Hi-Lo
aliases: Dubner / Braun / Wong / Thorp High-Low (blackjackreview row label)
Revere Plus-Minus (blackjackreview uses this label for Hi-Lo too; see Revere Advanced Plus-Minus)
systems.trueCountMethod: Running count divided by decks remaining (Wizard's example: RC +7 with 4 decks left gives 1.75, rounded to 2). Insurance at TC +3 or more (Wizard).
systems.publishedBcPeIc: QFIT table: BC .97, PE .51, IC .76. blackjackreview table: .97/.51/.76. BlackjackInfo calculator (Griffin EORs, 6D): PE 0.5114, BC 0.9682, IC 0.7601.
systems.notes: Wizard 6D sim (S17, DAS, surrender, I18+Fab4, bet raised only after wins): at 4.5 decks dealt, 1-5 +0.300% (SD 1.60, avg bet 1.41), 1-10 +0.587% (2.27, 1.68), 1-15 +0.834% (3.06, 1.90); at 5 decks dealt, 1-5 +0.469% (1.70, 1.47), 1-10 +0.837% (2.52, 1.80), 1-15 +1.147% (3.49, 2.10). Sweep A's '+1.182%, SD 3.54, avg bet 2.11 with full indexes' did not appear in my fetch of the page; treat as unverified. Sweep A's insurance counts from the blackjackreview 'i' page (1.5 SD, 2.4 DD, 3 shoe) were not re-fetched. Same tags as Hi-Lo Lite.

sources.what: TC = RC / decks remaining, insurance at TC +3, 6D simulation table

systems.name: Hi-Lo Lite
systems.trueCountMethod: Running count converted to a true count per deck. Indexes are grouped into five blocks: +1, +5, -1, -5, +10. Insurance sits in the +1 block.
systems.publishedBcPeIc: None published separately. The tags equal Hi-Lo's, so BC and IC equal Hi-Lo's (QFIT .97/.76).
systems.notes: A simplified index set on Hi-Lo tags, not new tags. Snyder's single-deck test (100M hands, 1-4 spread): Wong's complete Hi-Lo +1.32%, Hi-Lo Lite (39 indexes) +1.29%. The +1 insurance block looks tuned for single deck. For a tag-only EV engine this is a duplicate of Hi-Lo; it differs only if the engine models this index set.

sources.what: Snyder, Blackjack Forum Vol. XI #3 (Sept 1991): tags, per-deck TC, index blocks, insurance +1, 39-index version
Casino Verite lists 'Snyder Hi-Lo Lite' index set

systems.name: KO (Knock-Out)
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Deck sum +4 checked. Standard IRC = 4 - (4 x decks): 0 (1D), -4 (2D), -20 (6D), -28 (8D) per the authors, so the pack ends at +4. The 4D value is -12 by the same formula. Pivot = IRC + 4 x decks = +4 (BlackjackInfo forum), roughly a Hi-Lo TC of +4. Key count for 2D is +1 (authors' sample chapter). Sweep A also cites secondary key counts from bonusinsider (+2 1D, -4 6D, -6 8D) and insurance at RC +3; I did not re-fetch those. The authors allow shifting the IRC to avoid negative numbers.
systems.trueCountMethod: None. The authors say unbalancing removes the true-count conversion; decisions use the running count.
systems.publishedBcPeIc: QFIT table: .98/.55/.78. blackjackreview: .98/.55/.78. BlackjackInfo calculator (tags centred): PE 0.5530, BC 0.9770, IC 0.7832. Sweep A cites Modern Blackjack p.174: Rookie BC .98 with PE/IC blank (not re-fetched).
systems.notes: Same tags as REKO. Sweep A's extra aliases (All Sevens Count, T-Hop Basic, ESP-U) were not re-verified.

sources.what: Vancura & Fuchs sample chapter: +1 for 2-7, -1 for 10/J/Q/K/A, IRC = 4 - (4 x decks), 2D key count +1, no true count
pivot = 4 x decks + IRC; approximately Hi-Lo TC +4

systems.name: REKO (Ridiculously Easy Knock-Out)
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Deck sum +4 checked. Published IRCs (Modern Blackjack p.71): -1 (1D), -5 (2D), -12 (4D), -20 (6D), -27 (8D). These are not a fixed-pivot formula: IRC + 4 x decks = +3, +3, +4, +4, +5 respectively. It differs from KO at 1, 2 and 8 decks.
systems.trueCountMethod: None; running count only. One index value, +2, is used for every play at every deck count (QFIT REKO page). Sweep A's claim that insurance is also at +2 (p.73) was not confirmed by my fetch of p.73, which says only to insure when the count is high.
systems.publishedBcPeIc: QFIT table: .98/.55/.78. Modern Blackjack p.172: .98/.55/.78.
systems.notes: Wattenberger's own system on his own site, so primary. Same tags as KO; it differs only in IRCs and indexes.

sources.what: tags, single index +2, same power as KO Preferred, author Norm Wattenberger

systems.name: Red Seven (Red 7)
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Suit-aware: red 7 = +1, black 7 = 0; 0.5 is the per-rank average. Deck sum +2 checked. IRC = -2 x decks: -2 (1D), -4 (2D), -12 (6D), -16 (8D), so the pack ends at 0. At pivot 0 the advantage is up about 1% from the start (Snyder), roughly a balanced TC of +2. Raise bets at RC 0 or higher. Insurance at RC 0 or more in 1-2 deck games, +2 or more in shoes.
systems.publishedBcPeIc: QFIT table: .98/.54/.78 (7 shown as 0/1). blackjackreview: .98/.54/.78 (7 shown as .5). BlackjackInfo calculator (7 = 0.5): PE 0.5423, BC 0.9833, IC 0.7804.
systems.notes: ENGINE WARNING: a rank-only engine with 7 = 0.5 is not the real count; it changes the count's distribution. For exact EV, model red 7s (2 per deck, +1) and black 7s (2 per deck, 0) as separate card types.

sources.what: Snyder's own article: tags, red/black 7 rule, IRC by decks, pivot, betting and insurance

systems.notes: Humble & Cooper. Compute the with- and without-ace-side-count variants separately; the side count only raises BC.

sources.what: ace side-count procedure; Hi-Opt I listed as ace-neutral

systems.name: Unbalanced Zen 2 (UBZ2)
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Deck sum +4 checked. The IRC is UNRESOLVED; George C.'s 1995 booklet was not accessed. BJInfo's community 'Open Source UBZ II' table gives -4 x decks (-4 1D, -8 2D, -24 6D), pivot 0, 6D key count -6. That is the only choice with a deck-independent pivot (0), and it fits Renzey's forum remark that the pivot is +2 true (level-2 count). Several secondary sites say -2 x decks, and Casino Verite has index sets labelled 'starting at -2' and 'starting at 0'. With -2 x decks there is no fixed pivot (IRC + 4 x decks = 2 x decks).
systems.publishedBcPeIc: QFIT: .97/.62/.84. blackjackreview gives lower values: .94/.61/.82 (SUM 4).
systems.notes: The tags are confirmed. The IRC only shifts the running count, so an engine that sets its own bet ramp on a pivot-normalised count is unaffected; one that reproduces the booklet's key counts is affected.

sources.what: IRC -4/-8/-24, key count -6, pivot 0 (community open-source version)

systems.name: KISS I
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Suit- and face-aware: black 2s +1 and red 2s 0; J, Q and K -1; the 10-spot 0; 4, 5 and 6 +1. Deck sum +2 checked (matches blackjackreview SUM 2). The published IRC and key count were not found.
systems.aceSideCount: None; the ace is not counted.
systems.publishedBcPeIc: blackjackreview: .87/.58/.81. Not in the QFIT table.
systems.notes: Renzey's own post resolves the conflict with CasinoGuardian (2 = 0, all tens -1): blackjackreview's reading is correct. ENGINE WARNING: T = -0.75 and 2 = 0.5 are averages. For exact EV, split tens into the 10-spot (4 per deck, 0) and faces (12 per deck, -1), and 2s into black (+1) and red (0).

systems.name: KISS III
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Black 2s +1, red 2s 0. Deck sum +2 checked. IRCs quoted on Wizard of Vegas as from Blackjack Bluebook II: 18 (1D), 17 (2D), 9 (6D); key count always 20 (Renzey, quoted). The poster's written formula '21 - (6 x decks)' does not reproduce these numbers; 21 - 2 x decks gives 17 and 9, with 1D an exception at 18. Unshifted equivalent: IRC -2 x decks with pivot 0, like Red 7. The shifted form has pivot 21, and key count 20 sits one below it.

systems.notes: The IRCs come from a forum quotation of the book, not the book itself. ENGINE WARNING: model black and red 2s separately.

systems.name: Ten Count (unbalanced; insurance-oriented)
aliases: Archer / Goldberg / Hecher / One-Two / J. Noir (blackjackreview 'Archer' row label)
Optimal insurance count, Griffin -9/+4 (the balanced form of the same count)
systems.initialRunningCountAndPivot: Deck sum +4 checked. Wong 1981 via QFIT: start at 0 and insure when the count exceeds 4 x the number of decks in the game. Check: with IRC 0, count > 4n exactly when remaining tens are more than 1/3 of remaining cards, so insurance is perfect. Equivalent: IRC -4n, insure when RC > 0.
systems.trueCountMethod: For insurance, compare the RC with 4 x total decks. Thorp's and Revere's original ten counts used a ratio of non-tens to tens (Sweep A, via Wizard).
systems.publishedBcPeIc: blackjackreview 'Archer' row: BC .72, PE .61, IC 1.0. QFIT: -9/+4 tags are perfect for insurance (no numbers).
systems.notes: Any count with two tag values is an affine transform of any other. -9/+4 = (13/3) x (this count) - 1/3 per card, so it carries identical information; it is folded in here rather than listed separately.

sources.what: Wong 1981 ten count (-2 / +1) and insurance rule; -9/+4 perfect insurance count

systems.publishedBcPeIc: blackjackreview 'Uston Ace-Five': BC .54, PE .05, IC 0.0. Wizard gives none.
